newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up, rebounds on firm cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up, rebounds on firm cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Tuesday, rebounding from Monday's weakness on firm cash market prices in the western U.S., brokers and traders said.
"It seems like a bit of a bounce," said a New York-based broker.
Anticipation of heating demand in the Northwest and a rally in natural gas prices bolstered the physical electricity prices in the West, they said.
"Cash is still hanging in the $19.00 (a megawatt hour)," said a Northwest power trader, referring to electricity prices at the California-Oregon Border (COB) for Wednesday delivery.
He added that forecasts of very cool temperatures in parts of the Northwest would trigger space heating in the evening hours.
November natgas prices at the San Juan/Blanco Hub in New Mexico finished today at $1.95-$2.00 per million BTUs.
Today's natgas rally stemmed from concerns over a tropical depression forming in the Caribbean, which could move into the U.S. Gulf, and disrupt the region's natgas production.
November COB futures settled up 34 cents at $17.40 after being traded between $17.25-$17.50. December COB ended 15 cents to $18.75. Deferred COB contracts also finished higher.
November PV futures settled up 37 cents at $16.85, near its session high of $16.90. December PV ended up 65 cents at $17.40. Other PV months finished five to 60 cents higher.
Participants were split whether today's rise could be sustained. "I'm cautiously optimistic," said the broker.
Brokers and traders figured November COB futures need to surpass $17.50 and November PV needs to breach $17.00 to gain technical strength for a sustainable climb.
